import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between petal length and petal width,
# colored by species. This pair of features typically shows the best separation among Iris species.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',  # Color points by species
    s=100,          # Set marker size
    alpha=0.8,      # Set transparency
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend to identify species
plt.legend(title='Species', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='10')

# Add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
